publicReleaseNotes: Uptime 0.5.10 adds resumable, digest-checked archive transfers and a shared admission limit of 500 monitors. Repeat an interrupted rer export or rer import with the same absolute archive path after verifying a second factor and supplying a current session; changed input files and different installations or owners are refused. Large records and erasure journals travel in chunks. Restored monitors stay paused and delivery quarantined. Chunk transfers accept up to 64 MiB of encoded payload and one million rows per table; the ordinary console JSON archive route keeps its 2 MiB and 10,000-row bounds. These are refusal bounds, not measured capacity: bounded-memory restore and 500 monitors with 90 days of history are not established, and time-range selection and console chunk-transfer controls remain unavailable. Agents can edit internal incident notes with current-version and native permission checks, retaining history without mentions. API manual-check approval now accounts for all saved cleanup steps. Redirect refusals no longer reuse the previous hop's HTTP status in failure snapshots. The owner API can review and explicitly confirm disclosing one named Auth0 tenant domain to its fixed official RSS endpoint for a diagnostic source check; a changed tenant requires a new review. Auth0 status remains Unknown and cannot be followed. No migration or new required settings; monitors, history, incidents, destinations and private settings are kept on upgrade. The pinned @runeditrun/rer stays at 0.2.108; update an existing checkout with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile. Known issues: heartbeat output saved by 0.5.6 or earlier is not rewritten, so rotate a key earlier output may have contained; pattern-based redaction can still miss an unlabelled secret of no recognizable shape that is not listed under Output text to mask. A monitor CSV exported from UptimeRobot still cannot be imported. Restoring an archive does not restore the list of erased people, so pairing again with a Business that still lists them could invite them again. A company with a signed agent policy but no company settings receives an empty decision feed rather than a refusal. Response bodies over 64 KiB still fail the check; monitor a smaller health endpoint. Other earlier release limits remain. The product screenshot was taken on 0.4.0, before the console changes of 0.5.0 through 0.5.8. Product screenshot: .github/assets/release/uptime-0.4.0-monitor-1440.png
